items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We arrived at Bombay the 2nd of November... We were met by the manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel who was a Mr. Faletti... and two Negro musicians... Cricket Smith... and the other was Rudy Jackson

ctx.x: The whole voyage was wonderful and I felt as though I was living in wonderland. We arrived at Bombay the 2nd of November, ten sailing days from Venice. We were met by the manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel who was a Mr. Faletti, an Italian who was a naturalised English citizen, and two Negro musicians who were living in India and were going to play with the Abbey band. One was Cricket Smith, a trumpet player and the other was Rudy Jackson, an alto sax man. Cricket and Rudy had come to Europe in the early 20s.

We has seen many exciting things in the port towns we visited but Bombay gassed them all. The taxis were opened top five passenger cars, mostly American made, and I could see in front, on the sides and from the back without any difficulties. There were so many sights to see that I almost had a sore neck turning it so much from the time we left the port until we reached the Taj Mahal Hotel. One sees different events in newsreels and also movies about India which are very interesting but when you see these things…

The "Taj" was a very large and beautiful place which sat on a street overlooking the bay. The front faces the city and I learned later that the architect that drew the plans for the hotel commited suicide after the hotel was completed because the back of the hotel was built facing the bay and it should have been the opposite.
